outcome: Provision of neuraxial anesthesia (NA) during labor
Appropriate use of NA for elective/ESCS
Appropriate use of NA for vaginal deliveries
Provider responsiveness to objections to NA
cohort: 6391 women with migration history (first and second generations) and non-immigrant women giving birth in three obstetric hospitals in Berlin, Germany
finding: The study found evidence of underprovision of neuraxial anesthesia (NA) during labor among first-generation immigrants, women with low German language proficiency, and women with low educational attainment, but no evidence of overprovision.
mod_finding: There was no evidence for overprovision of care to immigrant women, either inappropriately (general anaesthesia for ESCS) or because of low provider responsiveness (no opt-out for NA in vaginal delivery).
